summary: Iteration 3: comprehensive admin-panel testing for the Bengali Islamic Institute. Backend pytest: 69/69 passing across 3 files (test_bii_api regression 18, test_upload 8, test_admin_panel new 43). Frontend Playwright: super_admin login → /home → sidebar sb-admin → /admin AdminLayout grouped sidebar verified; all 40+ admin sub-routes load and render admin-layout without page errors; student details modal works (shows enrollments, login history, complaints); all generic CRUD endpoints, all config PUT/GET endpoints, password-reset full flow, /api/maintenance-status public, /api/backup/export (password_hash redacted), analytics counts, teachers/admins CRUD with auto student_id 'T...', role enforcement (student → 403) all green. Two critical 500s fixed during testing: POST /api/teachers and POST /api/admins were returning ObjectId-serialization 500s because `_id` was not popped after insert_one — fix applied (server.py L975, L1034).

minor.issue: Returned 500 'ObjectId not iterable' because _id was not stripped from the dict after insert_one. FIXED during this iteration by adding doc.pop('_id', None) before return.

issues: Sidebar testid for the dashboard ('/admin') is computed as `adm-nav-admin` (because '/admin'.split('/').pop() === 'admin'), but spec/comment expected `adm-nav-dash`. Minor naming inconsistency — affects test discoverability only; visual link works.

Form input elements have placeholder-based labels but no `name` attribute, which means automated tests must select by placeholder or DOM order. Adding name attrs (e.g. name='text_bn', name='reference', name='primary_color', name='email') would improve testability.

action_items: OPTIONAL: rename AdminLayout dashboard NavLink testid from `adm-nav-admin` to `adm-nav-dash` (or compute end-route testid explicitly) so it matches the convention.
OPTIONAL: add `name` attributes to form inputs in CrudResource / AdminTeachers / ConfigEditor so QA can target them by name. Currently only placeholders are present.
critical_code_review_comments: Two endpoints (POST /api/teachers, POST /api/admins) leaked `_id` in the dict returned from FastAPI, causing 500 serialization errors. The pattern in generic register_crud already does `body.pop('_id', None)` — make this a helper and apply consistently to ALL endpoints that insert + return docs.

server.py is now ~1348 lines and continues to mix models + routes + storage + seed. Strongly recommend splitting into routers/(auth, admin, users, crud, configs, files, backup), models.py, storage.py, seed.py.
Still no brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (carried over from iter 1 & 2). Playbook recommends 5-fail lockout.
Password reset flow returns reset_code directly in response (`mocked:true`). Acceptable for now but must be replaced with real email delivery before launch.
Generic CRUD POST accepts an arbitrary `dict` — no Pydantic validation. Acceptable for admin-only writes but worth tightening per-resource (e.g. hadiths should require text_bn or reference).

register_config endpoints expose any config as public via GET — this is intentional and useful (theme/maintenance) but a malicious user could read e.g. /api/configs/firebase or /api/configs/payment_gateways which may contain secrets. STRONG RECOMMENDATION: gate /api/configs/firebase, /api/configs/payment_gateways, /api/configs/security behind admin auth.

GET /api/backup/export correctly strips password_hash, but it also dumps ALL collections including configs (which may carry sensitive payment_gateways / firebase keys). Consider redacting sensitive config keys before export.

Maintenance mode flag is checked only via /api/maintenance-status — the backend does not actually block API requests when enabled. Either enforce a middleware that returns 503 for non-admins when enabled, or document that maintenance is only a UI-side banner.
delete_admin uses filter {role:'admin'} so it will silently no-op (deleted=0) when trying to delete a super_admin, rather than returning a clear 400 error.
test_credentials.md still references legacy `/api/auth/change-password`, `/api/auth/logout`, `/api/upload` — these continue to work; just keeping the file accurate is good practice.

rca of the issue: RCA — POST /api/teachers and POST /api/admins 500: Motor's insert_one mutates the input dict by injecting `_id: ObjectId(...)`. The handlers then returned that same dict via FastAPI, which tried to serialize ObjectId → ValueError. Reproduction: POST /api/teachers with super_admin token → 500 'ObjectId not iterable'. Mitigation: added `doc.pop('_id', None)` immediately after insert_one (before return). The generic register_crud factory already did this; only the custom teacher/admin endpoints had missed it. After fix, both endpoints return 200 with clean JSON, validated by tests TestTeachers.test_crud and TestAdmins.test_list_and_create.
